matches.heading: ### S14 — An injective map needs an algebraic splitting
matches.excerpt: The previous isomorphism argument cannot simply be applied to an injection between spaces of different dimensions, because no inverse exists on the whole target. The corner containing \(g\) is the required algebraic left inverse; surjections are treated with the opposite equation. matches.heading: ### R12 — Unproved claim: a later compatibility check remains explicitly unfinished
matches.excerpt: The published continuation asks for compatibility between the discriminant pairing and the cohomological construction, and Remark 8.5 acknowledges that this verification has not been carried out (Grothendieck, 1968, pp. 150–151). Thus the elementary matrix calculation in R4 does not by itself establish that compatibility. A reconstruction must compare the cycle class, Kummer boundary, cup product, and local trace maps with their signs, rather than merely exhibit two perfect pairings on abstractly isomorphic finite groups.

matches.heading: ### R13 — Unpursued implication: distinguish negative definiteness from the full local duality assertion
matches.excerpt: Mumford (1961, p. 6) proves negative definiteness of the exceptional intersection matrix in the setting of a resolved normal complex surface singularity. His discussion also identifies the matrix cokernel with a torsion group arising from the link (pp. 10–11), offering a concrete comparison for the finite quotient on this sheet. Neither that complex topological interpretation nor the elementary discriminant calculation alone establishes the stated étale-duality compatibility in the more general algebraic situation; the hypotheses and comparison maps remain part of the research problem.

matches.heading: ### S13 — Positivity kills the radical once the rational algebra is finite
matches.excerpt: Let a finite-dimensional rational algebra \(R\) have a faithful finite-dimensional realization, an involution \(*\), a rational-valued trace, and \(\operatorname{Tr}(x^*x)>0\) for every nonzero \(x\in R\); its Jacobson radical is involution-stable and nilpotent, so \(x^*x\) has trace zero for \(x\) in the radical, forcing that radical to vanish. matches.heading: ### F15 — Cote 47, scan 9, question about torsion
matches.excerpt: A useful later comparison distinguishes a particular bundle’s integral Chern classes from an integral Fourier transform on the entire Chow group. Beckmann and de Gaay Fortman (2023, Theorem 3.8) characterize integral lifts of the Poincaré character using a specific one-cycle; under a symmetric ample principal polarization, they also relate this to preservation of Chow groups modulo torsion and to weak integral Fourier transforms. These additional hypotheses and the distinction between rational identities and integral lifts prevent the manuscript’s local heuristic from being treated as a general integral-transform theorem.
